---
title: "Setup guide"
---

You'll do your coding in **GitHub Codespaces**: the course's Python setup, running
on GitHub's computers and shown in your web browser. There's nothing to install,
and it works the same on any laptop, a Chromebook, or a campus lab computer.
Do steps 1–5 before the second class session. If you get stuck, see the
[Setup FAQ](setup-faq.qmd).

Prefer a desktop editor or working offline? You can also
[work on your own computer](setup-local.qmd). That's optional, and you can add it
any time.

**Before you start:** an internet connection, a current web browser (Chrome,
Edge, Firefox, or Safari), and your phone for GitHub's sign-in codes.

## One-time setup

1. **GitHub**: the website that stores your course work online. Each student gets a private repository ("repo") there, a folder only you and the instructor can see. New problem sets arrive in it. To hand in work, you use Git to save it to your repo, then submit the link to it in Canvas.
   - Sign up at [github.com](https://github.com) with any username (it doesn't need to be your real name), and add your WSU email to the account.
   - Apply for GitHub Education student benefits at [education.github.com](https://education.github.com). Approval can take a few days; it gives you free GitHub Copilot and free Codespaces hours.
   - GitHub will ask you to set up two-factor sign-in. Keep that phone or app handy: you'll need a code when you sign in on a lab computer.
   - Enter your GitHub username in the Canvas "GitHub username" survey, so your course repo can be created.

2. **Accept your repo invitation** from the email GitHub sends you, or at
   `https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>/invitations`.

3. **Create your codespace.** On your repo's page
   (`https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>`), click the green
   **Code** button, choose the **Codespaces** tab, and click **Create codespace on
   main**.
   - The first time takes a few minutes while it installs Python and the course
     packages. Then an editor opens in your browser. It's VS Code, the program
     Positron is built on.
   - If it offers to turn on GitHub Copilot or AI code completions, skip it for
     now. AI autocomplete stays off through Week 5 (see [Policies](policies.qmd)).

4. **Check it.** Open a terminal: click the **☰** menu at the top left, then
   **Terminal > New Terminal** (or press **Ctrl+`**). Run:

   ```bash
   uv run python check_setup.py
   ```

   Every line should start with `[OK]`.

5. **Do PS01.** In the file list on the left, open `ps01/ps01.ipynb`. If the
   notebook asks you to **Select Kernel** (top right), choose **Python
   Environments**, then the one in `.venv`. Complete it, then:
   - In **Source Control** (the branching icon on the left), type a short
     message such as "PS01 done" in the box and click **Commit**. Every commit
     needs a message.
   - Click **Sync Changes** to push it to GitHub.
   - On your repo's GitHub page, open the commit, copy its URL, and paste it into
     the PS01 assignment in Canvas.

## Each time you work {#each-time}

- **Open your codespace:** your repo's page > **Code** > **Codespaces** tab >
  click the codespace that's already there. Reuse it; don't create a new one
  each time.
- **Start by pulling:** in Source Control, click **Sync Changes** (or **⋯ > Pull**)
  so you have any new problem sets.
- **Before you leave: commit and push.** Your work is only safe once it's on
  GitHub. A codespace you stop using for a few weeks is deleted, and anything
  not pushed goes with it.
- **Then close the tab.** The codespace stops by itself after 30 idle minutes.
  To stop it right away, go to [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces),
  click **⋯** next to it, and choose **Stop codespace**.
- **On a lab or shared computer,** sign out of GitHub when you're done.

**Your monthly allowance:** your GitHub account includes about 60 hours of
codespace time a month, or 90 once your student benefits are approved. That's
plenty for this course if you stop your codespace when you're done. You can see
your usage under **Settings > Billing** on GitHub.

## Every problem set

1. **Pull** (Source Control > **Sync Changes**). The new `psNN/` folder appears.
2. **Work** in `psNN/psNN.ipynb`, and commit whenever something works.
3. **Restart & Run All.** If it doesn't run from top to bottom, it isn't finished.
4. **Fill in the AI usage note** at the bottom.
5. **Commit, push (Sync Changes), copy the commit URL** from GitHub, and **paste
   it into Canvas** before the deadline.

## Rules of the road {#rules}

- Your repo is private. Never make it public or share it, even after the course,
  unless an assignment says it may be shared.
- Use relative paths (`data/prices.csv`), never full paths like `C:\Users\...`
  or `/workspaces/...`. Your code must run on the instructor's machine.
- Don't commit `.venv/` or big data files. GitHub rejects files over 100 MB, and
  your repo's `.gitignore` handles the common cases.
- Don't change `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`. If you think you need another
  package, ask on Discussions.
- **Asking for help:** see [Getting help](setup-faq.qmd#getting-help).
